steps.prompt: The AMC 10 gives you $75$ minutes for $25$ problems. Would you rather spend $10$ minutes cracking problem $20$, or use them to check problems $1$ to $10$? Why?

cards.title: How the AMC 10 is scored
cards.body: $25$ problems, $75$ minutes, choices (A) to (E). A right answer scores $6$, a blank $1.5$ and a wrong answer $0$. The problems get harder as you go, but every problem is worth the same $6$ points: an easy problem you get right counts as much as the hardest one.

cards.title: The pacing plan and the 2-minute rule
cards.body: Plan two passes. First pass: work through in order. If a problem has no clear plan after $2$ minutes, flag it, skip it and move on. Aim to finish the first pass with about $25$ minutes left. Second pass: go back to the flagged problems, most promising first. Save $3$ to $5$ minutes at the end to check your answer sheet.

cards.title: Worked example: the time budget
cards.problem: Your first pass works $18$ problems at about $2.5$ minutes each. How much time is left for the $7$ skipped problems?

try.prompt: How many minutes is the first pass?

steps.text: That leaves $75 - 45 = 30$ minutes for $7$ problems: plenty for a second look.

cards.title: Guess or leave it blank?
cards.body: A blank is worth $1.5$ points. A wild guess among $5$ choices is worth $\frac{6}{5} = 1.2$ points on average, less than a blank. Rule out one choice and a guess is worth $\frac{6}{4} = 1.5$, a tie; rule out two and it is worth $2$. So: leave it blank unless you can rule out at least two choices.

cards.title: Worked example: is it worth guessing?
cards.problem: You've ruled out $2$ choices. What is a guess worth on average?

steps.text: $3$ choices are left, so you're right with probability $\frac{1}{3}$.
$6 \times \frac{1}{3} = 2$ points, more than the $1.5$ for a blank: guess.

try.prompt: How many points is the guess worth?

prompts: What is your pacing plan for the first pass and the second pass?
